name: Pierre Auger Observatory
summary: Hybrid ultrahigh-energy cosmic-ray observatory in Argentina. Alongside cosmic-ray origins and composition, the collaboration uses ultrahigh-energy photon and neutrino searches to test superheavy-dark-matter models. AugerPrime is an upgrade phase of the same observatory.
detection_principle: A surface water-Cherenkov array measures extensive-air-shower particles, while fluorescence telescopes measure longitudinal development. Waveform timing, lateral distributions and muon content separate photon from hadron showers; photon-flux upper limits are then interpreted in specified superheavy-dark-matter models.

key_parameters.name: Energy thresholds in the cited photon search

phases.name: Baseline hybrid observatory
phases.description: Long-term data taking with the water-Cherenkov array and fluorescence telescopes; the example result here uses only 2004–2020 data.

phases.name: AugerPrime
phases.description: Improves electromagnetic / muon separation. The 2025 report describes added scintillators, radio antennas, electronics and underground muon detectors.

results.summary: For a diffuse photon flux with an assumed E^-2 spectrum, 95% CL upper limits above 10^19, 2×10^19 and 4×10^19 eV are respectively 2.11×10^-3, 3.12×10^-4 and 1.72×10^-4 km^-2 sr^-1 yr^-1. The paper discusses superheavy-dark-matter constraints; flux limits alone are not model-independent dark-matter-lifetime bounds.

science_scope: Multipurpose cosmic-ray observatory included on the basis of the collaboration's original photon searches and their superheavy-dark-matter interpretation. Identifying an air shower as an ordinary cosmic ray or rare photon does not identify a dark-matter particle; mass, decay channel and Galactic-halo model affect lifetime limits.
